newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU council must not interfere with ECB - de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EMU council must not interfere with ECB - de Silguy.

text.p: European Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday a stability council for the euro-zone could be a good thing but that it should not interfere in the monetary policies of the future European Central Bank.
He also said such a council, originally proposed by France, should be informal and that it was important to keep the balance between the EU's institutions as laid down by the bloc's treaty.

"This council should remain very informal and should not in any circumstances interfere in the conduct of monetary policy which is the competence...of the European Central Bank," he told a briefing with Swedish journalists ahead of a visit to Sweden.
"Under these conditions this stability council, a institution in which one could hold discussions, get to know each other better,...is a good thing," he said.
The council must not be used to keep the Commission out of decision-making, he added.

He stressed that decisions were taken by EU finance ministers in ECOFIN and that decisions on the Euro would be taken by finance ministers of those countries that participate in EMU, but within the framework of the ECOFIN.
On Wednesday, France and Germany reaffirmed their support for an informal stability council to oversee economic policies in the euro-zone after the launch of the single currency.
The idea came under attack earlier this year, notably from some members of the German Bundesbank who feared it might be used to undermine the independence of the ECB.
This council would in no way threaten the independence of the ECB, to which France was fully committed, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said at the meeting in Lyon on Wednesday.
And though it would be like the Group of Seven in its informality, unlike the G7 it would not make proposals on exchange rate levels, nor include central bank governors.
